title: The Almost Playlist
premise: Cyrus Amberdale has spent two years at Hollow Creek High keeping her head down, still grieving the sister whose death the town quietly buried. When a group chat called The Almost Playlist begins sending her songs that predict small tragedies before they happen, she realizes the messages are coming from someone who knows what really happened to her sister—and that the school was built over the old Bellamy estate where it happened. As the predictions escalate from pranks to danger, Cyrus must choose between protecting her new friends and exposing the beloved teacher who caused the accident everyone covered up. In the end, she broadcasts the truth through the playlist itself, losing her closest friendship but finally reclaiming her own name, memory, and future.
about_author: R. M. Crane is a former high school archivist who grew up in a mill town where half the buildings had older foundations than their plaques admitted. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to let towns forget.

chapters.title: Day 412 of the Sentence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She counts down days to graduation, invisible by design, sketching in the margins of her notebook while teachers praise her quietness. A fire drill interrupts third period—oddly, before any alarm sounds. Emotional beat: numb routine cracked by the first hairline fracture of something wrong.

chapters.title: Unknown Number, Known Song
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. An invite to a group chat called The Almost Playlist appears on her phone; no one admits to adding her. The first message is a song title—'Smoke Signals'—sent an hour before the gym trash can catches fire. Beat: unease sharpening into attention; invisibility is starting to feel like a trap.

chapters.title: The Founders' Wing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Assigned to archive old yearbooks for service credit, she finds photos of the Bellamy estate that stood where the school now sits, and a 1998 page torn out. Her friend Dev jokes about ghosts; Cyrus doesn't laugh. Beat: curiosity kindled against her will.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows the Words
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus and Marisol POV. Marisol, charismatic and guarded, quotes the next predicted song before it arrives. She warns Cyrus not to reply to the chat. Beat: magnetic friendship forming over shared secrets neither will name.

chapters.title: Prediction Three: The Ice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The chat predicts a student will fall through the pond ice; Cyrus pulls Wren back from the edge minutes before the ice cracks. No one saw her do it—which means whoever runs the chat did. Beat: terror braided with purpose; she can't look away now.

chapters.title: What Happened to Juniper
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn her sister Juniper died at sixteen near the old Bellamy grounds, ruled an accident, and how Cyrus's family fractured around the silence. Beat: grief given shape; the stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Mr. Voss's Extra Credit
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Beloved history teacher Mr. Voss offers to help her research the Bellamy estate—too eagerly, she later thinks. He steers her away from 1998 records. Beat: trust established so it can be broken; dramatic irony begins.

chapters.title: The Playlist Grows Teeth
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via chat logs. Predictions turn crueler: a locker vandalism, a teacher's breakdown, each arriving like setlists for disasters. The group fractures—Dev wants out, Marisol wants answers. Beat: rising dread; the game has players, plural.

chapters.title: Wren Sees Her
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The girl Cyrus saved starts following her, convinced they're connected. Wren reveals her aunt worked at the Bellamy house and never spoke of it again. Beat: alliance forming; Cyrus is seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Basement of the Old House
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Marisol, and Wren break into the sealed sub-basement beneath the gym. They find a wall of cassette tapes labeled with dates—including the night Juniper died. Beat: revelation and violation; the past literally underfoot.

chapters.title: Track Seven
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She plays a tape: recorded audio of the night of the accident—voices, glass, a man saying 'we'll handle it.' The voice belongs to someone she knows. Beat: gut-punch recognition; justice stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Marisol's Lie
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. It emerges Marisol's family received hush money after her father's injury at the construction site; she joined the chat to control the story. Cyrus feels betrayed. Beat: friendship cracking under the weight of secrets kept 'to protect.'

chapters.title: The Chat Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The predictions stop mid-song. Then a private message: 'You're close. So are they.' Someone is watching her movements in real time. Beat: paranoia peaks; hunter and hunted blur.

chapters.title: Detention with Mr. Voss
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Voss gently suggests she's unwell, echoing what adults said about Juniper. He mentions the tapes should be 'returned.' Cyrus realizes he knows exactly what she found. Beat: gaslighting recognized and refused; her spine straightens.

chapters.title: The Almost Reunion
chapters.summary: Group POV. Cyrus reunites the fractured chat—Dev, Wren, even reluctant Marisol—to compare notes. Each prediction maps to dates in the torn-out 1998 yearbook page. Beat: collective resolve; the playlist becomes a map.

chapters.title: Fire Drill, Again
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A final prediction arrives: 'Last track. Fire. Friday assembly.' Cyrus realizes the chat isn't predicting—it's warning, and the sender is inside the building. Beat: countdown begins; dread becomes momentum.

chapters.title: Who Built the Playlist
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They trace the account to the school's original bell system wiring and suspect the janitor, Ellery—a Bellamy groundskeeper's son who's been leaving warnings for decades. But the evidence also points somewhere worse. Beat: misdirection resolved, true threat revealed.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Friday assembly. Voss announces a 'maintenance issue'; smoke already threads the auditorium vents. Cyrus must decide: evacuate quietly and stay safe, or use the microphone. Beat: the choice the whole book has been building toward.

chapters.title: Tell the Truth Even If It Costs
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, climax. She takes the mic, names Voss, describes the tape, as alarms finally sound. Chaos, evacuation, Voss cornered by his own recorded voice playing over the PA—Ellery's doing. Beat: catharsis; visibility chosen at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Parking Lot
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Voss is arrested; the town's version of events begins rewriting itself in real time. Marisol comes clean publicly, mending what she can. Dev stands apart—the friendship that doesn't survive. Beat: bittersweet accounting; truth's price itemized.

chapters.title: Juniper's Track
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Among the tapes is one labeled with Juniper's name: her sister's voice, laughing, singing, alive. Cyrus plays it for her parents and finally grieves out loud instead of counting days. Beat: mourning transformed into memory; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Graduation Day (Day Zero)
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue. She walks at graduation under her full name, Cyrus Amberdale, spoken aloud. The Almost Playlist sends one last message—not a prediction, just a song, and the words 'you made your own track.' Beat: resolution; the sentence served ends, and a life begins.
